scope_basis: Artificial intelligence lab building capacity in the Sahel.
title: RobotsMali AI4D Lab
description: Responsible artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to accelerate the transformation of Francophone countries in the Sahel region, but research and innovation capacity in this region is very weak compared to Anglophone African countries. Among the many challenges research institutions confront in the region is the basic one of language. Knowledge of English among students is very rare and constitutes a formidable barrier to developing competence in AI. The RobotsMali AI4D Lab seeks to build capacity within both public and private sectors to conduct local, relevant and multidisciplinary research aimed at contributing to the social and economic development of the region. The lab is a collaborative research hub and nexus of the major public universities of Mali, private universities, government, social organizations and industry. The lab will support multidisciplinary teams to research interventions that can improve educational outcomes and literacy, contribute to the enhancement of AI teaching and research capabilities in Francophone institutions of higher learning, and incubate AI-powered startups. The activities of the lab will revolve around the pillars of community-building and skill development, scientific rigour, commitment to ethical and responsible practices, gender equality and inclusion. This project is a part of the Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) program, a five-year partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office to support policy, innovations and expanded leadership to spur safe and responsible AI development in Africa. The vision of the new partnership is to support an inclusive, responsible AI ecosystem that improves quality of life for all in Africa and beyond.

scope_basis: Contribution co-funds the national population census.
title: Mali RGPH5 census — special review, Swedish contribution
description:
The Malian general census takes place every 10 years. The fifth census was planned to take place 2016-2021 with 2019 being the year when most of the work will be implemented. The process was delayed and concluded 2022. The census is a large and complicated project in a vast country like Mali that has limited infrastructure and security challenges. The census will produce data that will be used for social and economic development in the country and to follow up on development interventions.

The Swedish contribution will be used by the Malian government to co-fund the fifth population census (RGPH5) in Mali. By Malian law and according to UN recommendations these are to take place every 10 years. The census is not a sample but a complete inventory of people and their accommodation in Mali. The census will provide data and analyses on: 1) total number of inhabitants in Mali and structure by sex and age 2) spatial distribution of people according to administrative unites and type of residence 3) social, economic and cultural characteristics of the Malian population 4) level, structure and tendencies regarding fertility, civil status, mortality and migration 5) indicators for lobbying regarding vulnerable groups, especially old people, women, young people, people living with handicaps, displaced people, orphans etc 6) conclusions regarding the evolution of the data above since the 1976 census 7) projections and demographic prospects into the future 8) characteristics of households, habitat and livelihoods 9) analysis and cartography of poverty 10) updated statistics on villages, wells and other collective social infrastructure 11) geo-referenced information on collective social infrastructure and economic units 12) establishment of demographic indicators 13) capacity building on data collection, analysis and communication using modern information technology The intervention produces baseline information and analyses that are crucial to the design of development action,

Outcome: The competitiveness of the tech sector is increased in partner countries    Since mid-March 2020, we have been in regular contact with FastTrackTech beneficiaries to measure the impact of Covid 19 on their businesses. Most planned B2B activities were cancelled or postponed since traveling and public gatherings are restricted. 2020 Work Plans have been reviewed to adapt to the current situation, which will seriously impact our capacity to generate business and investment opportunities for our beneficiaries. CITCC is the contractor responsible for project implementation. In February 2019, Ambassador Zhu Liying visited the construction site and had a discussion with the head of the project team. scope_basis: Improves the national statistical system.
title: Improving Mali's Statistical System
description: The objective of the Improving Mali's Statistical System Project is to strengthen the capacity of the National Statistical System (NSS) to produce and publicly disseminate statistics through support to institutional development and data production. There are three components to the project, the first component being data collection, quality enhancement, and dissemination. This component will fund three sets of subcomponents: (a) foundational data collection (RGPH digital cartography, enterprise, and national accounts data); (b) technical assistance to enhance quality of routine data collection (agriculture and welfare data); and (c) data dissemination and analysis. These data production activities were selected based upon the following factors: (i) impact on the whole NSS and (ii) the quality of existing information. The second component is the institutional and human resources development. Statistical production in a decentralized system such as Mali is based on three essential pillars: the legal framework and the quality of statistical coordination, administrative and financial autonomy, and staff expertise. An enabling institutional environment for quality statistics requires incentives of actors to be aligned. This component aims to support institutional reforms through background studies (institutional and human resource assessments) and dialogues (between the CNS, Ministry of Finance, and Ministry of Population) to identify/strengthen reforms around the Government's performance budgeting initiative. Finally, the third component is the project management.

description: The importance of reliable data to allow for rational governance-related decisions has been recognized in Mali for a long time which is shown by a number of reforms within the national statistics system during the last fifteen years. Sweden and Mali is cooperating within the field since 2009 to strengthen the capacity in Mali to allow the country to produce reliable data that can contribute to development and poverty reduction. Sida has funded this work that is jointly implemented by Swedish SCB and their Malian counterpart INSTAT. The work contributes to the objectives Mali has established in its poverty reduction strategy, the Millennium Development Goals as well as the more recent Sustainable Development Goals. The objective is to produce reliable data and qualitative analyses that enable follow-up of development interventions. The framework for statistics in Mali has improved in recent years and the capacity of the institute has been strengthened as part of a national roadmap for statistics (SDS – Schema pour le Developpement Statistique). Via authority specific statistics units (CPS – Cellules de Production Statistique) the capacity within health, education and environmental statistics has been strengthened. The suggested intervention intends to continue this important work through two main components, one technical component where SCB will strengthen the capacity of INSTAT and a financial component with data collection, for instance via Permanent Modular Household Surveys (EMOP – Enquête Modulaire Permanente auprès des Ménages) and via improvement of statistical infrastructure. The first component, the technical one, is governed contractually by an agreement between the Embassy and SCB as well as a "tjänsteköpsavtal" and the second one, the financial one, by an agreement between the Embassy and INSTAT (signed by the Mali Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Focus among the sectors will continue to be on social and economic data but the intervention also includes capacity building regarding environmental statistics which is important for instance to adapt to climate change. The intervention also aims at strengthening INSTAT's capacity to produce, analyze and present gender disaggregated data. The intervention produces data on the different development needs of people in different parts of Mali which is necessary to avoid marginlization, prevent conflict and promote peace and security. Given the importance of good statistics and statistical analyses for good governance it is proposed that the embassy invests SEK 49 895 000 SEK including SEK 31 391 000 for technical support by SCB and SEK 18 504 000 SEK for financial support to INSTAT for the above-mentioned intervention.
